questions.q: Why does building a PivotTable from a real Excel Table beat building it from a raw range?
options: The PivotTable automatically expands to include new rows as the Table grows, with no source reference to manually fix
Tables make every PivotTable calculation faster, with no other benefit
There is no real difference between the two approaches
PivotTables can only technically be created from Tables, never from raw ranges
questions.explain: A Table-based PivotTable's Table/Range box references the Table by name, so newly added rows are automatically included after a refresh — a raw range stays fixed at whatever address was originally selected.

questions.q: What does Excel show when you go to Insert > PivotTable in current versions?
options: Nothing — Insert > PivotTable only works after a layout is manually coded
A blank worksheet with no guidance of any kind
An Insert PivotTable pane that proposes a recommended layout preview based on the source data's shape
A mandatory wizard that cannot be skipped or adjusted afterward
questions.explain: The Insert PivotTable pane shows a recommended layout preview (like 'Sales by Product and Year') as a helpful starting point — accepting it still produces a fully editable PivotTable.

questions.q: What are the four drop zones in the PivotTable Fields pane?
options: Filters, Rows, Columns, and Values
Source, Filters, Groups, and Totals
Rows, Columns, Formulas, and Charts
Headers, Footers, Filters, and Totals
questions.explain: Every PivotTable is structured from these four zones: Filters narrows the whole report, Rows and Columns group the data, and Values aggregates it.

questions.q: What happens by default when a numeric field is dragged into the Values zone?
options: It is automatically converted into a calculated field
It is displayed as raw, unaggregated individual values
It is moved into the Rows zone instead
It is aggregated, defaulting to Sum for numbers (Count for text fields)
questions.explain: Values doesn't just display a field — it aggregates it, defaulting to Sum for numeric data and Count for text, which is the foundation Lesson 14's calculated fields build on.

questions.q: What is a common PivotTable bug that a Table-based source avoids?
options: Raw ranges prevent the Filters zone from working
A source range that quietly stops short of the real data because rows were inserted below the original selection
PivotTables built from Tables cannot use the Values zone
PivotTables built from ranges always calculate incorrect totals
questions.explain: A fixed raw-range reference doesn't grow when new rows are added below it, silently excluding new data — a Table reference expands automatically, avoiding that exact bug.
